android_mechanism: Worker scheduling not adapted to the workload; fix parallelizes/adapts scheduling
bug_description: refreshAllFeeds fetches every due feed strictly sequentially (await per feed inside a for loop). Each fetch waits for the previous feed's full network round-trip and parse, so refreshing many subscriptions takes the SUM of all per-feed latencies instead of overlapping them.
fix_summary: Due feeds are fetched by a bounded worker pool (4 concurrent), overlapping network latency while limiting parallelism.

test_oracle.definition: on-CPU time of the app process during the measured step, from the sched events in trace.htrace.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.note: cpu 5420 vs 3930 ms (+38%, disjoint ranges); total instructions match because the same fetches run, so the oracle is sched CPU time

mechanism_oracle.definition: Wall time from refresh start to the last feed's completion, from network activity in the trace.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed total ~= sum of per-feed latencies (serialized request timeline); fixed overlaps up to 4 fetches. With 10+ feeds, fixed refresh time <= ~50% of unfixed.

reproduction: git -C hosts/sheafreader checkout case/sheafreader_refresh_feeds_sequential/unfixed; apply the measurement harness patch for this case, build, sign and install the HAP.
git -C hosts/sheafreader checkout case/sheafreader_refresh_feeds_sequential/fixed; rebuild, reinstall and repeat identically.
Compare test_oracle.metric across the two report sets: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed.
